subject.title: [Enhancement] Agent Tool Execution Safety: Forward Abort Signals to Before-Tool Hooks and Add Bounded Execution Timeouts

question: Should the global per-tool timeout and plugin override configuration be split from the narrow adapter cancellation and client-hook error-boundary repair?
rationale: The adapter omission is source-backed and bounded, while universal timeout defaults and public plugin cancellation semantics change product behavior and compatibility for long-running tools.

options.title: Split lifecycle from timeout policy
options.body: Implement signal forwarding and focused error semantics now, then track global timeout behavior in a separate owner-reviewed design.

options.title: Approve a combined execution policy
options.body: Keep one item but require explicit defaults, override ownership, upgrade behavior, and long-running-tool proof before implementation.

recommendation.title: Split lifecycle from timeout policy
recommendation.body: Implement signal forwarding and focused error semantics now, then track global timeout behavior in a separate owner-reviewed design.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main provenance ties the central adapter and hook implementation to his recent repository integration, making him the best available owner for the scope decision.
